Hind may take from miserly Abu Sufyan's property what is reasonable for her children, and a wife who gives charity from her husband's property unbidden earns him half the reward.
Fatima asked for a servant for her mill-worn hands; the Prophet taught her and Ali to say Subhan Allah and Al-hamdu lillah thirty-three times and Allahu Akbar thirty-four at bedtime.
Aisha said the Prophet worked for his family at home and went out when he heard the adhan.
Hind, whose husband Abu Sufyan gave her too little, was told she may take what suffices her and her children, in a just and reasonable amount.
The best women among camel riders are of Quraysh, the righteous of them kind to their young children and careful of their husbands' property.
Ali wore a silk suit the Prophet gave him, then, seeing anger on his face, cut it up and shared it among his womenfolk.
Jabir, whose father left seven or nine daughters, married a matron rather than a virgin so she could look after them, and the Prophet blessed him.
Unable to free a slave, fast two months or feed sixty poor after intercourse while fasting in Ramadan, a man was given dates as expiation and allowed to keep them.
Umm Salama is rewarded for spending on Abu Salama's children, and Hind may take from miserly Abu Sufyan's property what she and her children reasonably need.
The Prophet left the funeral prayer of debtors who left nothing to others, but after Allah gave him victories he paid believers' debts himself, their wealth going to heirs.
The Prophet declined to marry Umm Habiba's sister, unlawful to him, or Umm Salama's daughter, his foster niece through Thuwaiba, and asked not to be offered daughters and sisters.
Feed the hungry, visit the sick and free captives; Muhammad's family never ate their fill three days running, and the Prophet fed a starving Abu Huraira milk until full.
The Prophet told his stepson Umar bin Abi Salama to say Allah's name, eat with his right hand and from what is nearest; he liked starting from the right.
Abu Talha's few barley loaves, blessed by the Prophet, fed eighty men in tens, and one sheep fed all 130 men with some left over.
The Prophet's household lived on dates and water, near Khaibar only sawiq; he ate no thin bread and not at tables but on leather sheets, as at Safiyya's wedding.
Taunted as son of the woman of two waist-belts, Ibn az-Zubair heard from Asma that she split her belt to tie the Prophet's water skin and food container.
Mastigure meat, not unlawful, was eaten on the Prophet's dining sheet though he disliked it, not being of his people's land; at As-Sahba they ate only sawiq.
Food for two suffices three and for three suffices four; a believer eats in one intestine and a disbeliever in seven; a man ate less after embracing Islam.
The Prophet did not eat while leaning, and withdrew his hand from roasted mastigure, not unlawful but not found in his people's land, while Khalid ate it.
At Itban's house, where the Prophet prayed, he told a man calling Malik a hypocrite that the Fire is forbidden to whoever sincerely testifies that none but Allah deserves worship.
The Prophet drank milk and ate iqt but left the mastigures set on his dining sheet; Sahl's companions relished an old woman's silq and barley dish after Friday prayer.
The Prophet bit meat off a shoulder, stripped the foreleg of Abu Qatada's onager though in Ihram, and cut mutton with a knife, praying afterwards without renewing ablution.
The Prophet never criticised food; they had no white flour or sieves and ate unsifted barley, dates or leaves; his family never ate wheat bread their fill three days running.
When a relative died, Aisha had talbina served to the women, citing the Prophet's saying that talbina soothes the patient's heart and eases some sadness.
Many men reached perfection but among women only Mary, daughter of Imran, and Asia, Pharaoh's wife; Aisha excels other women as tharid excels other food.
The Prophet picked gourd from a tailor's tharid, never saw thin bread or a roasted sheep, Anas said, and cut mutton with a knife, praying without new ablution.
The Prophet barred keeping sacrifice meat beyond three days only in a year of hunger, so the rich would feed the poor; later it was stored and carried to Medina.
Anas, serving the Prophet, often heard him seek refuge from worry and debt; returning from Khaibar he held Safiyya's wedding feast, said Uhud loves us, and declared Medina a sanctuary.
Hudhaifa threw back the cup a Magian brought him, citing the Prophet's ban on silk and on eating or drinking from gold or silver vessels, the unbelievers' in this world.
A believer reciting the Quran is like a citron, one not reciting like a date; a hypocrite reciting is like a fragrant bitter plant, one not reciting like colocynth.
The Prophet said Aisha excels other women as tharid excels other kinds of food.
Travel is a kind of torment, keeping one from sleep and food, so when one's business is done, one should hurry back to one's family.
Three rulings came through Barira: wala goes to whoever frees, once freed she might keep or leave her husband, and charity meat given her was a gift to the Prophet.
The Prophet loved sweets and honey; hungry Abu Huraira sought meals and praised Ja'far's kindness to the poor; the Prophet ate gourd at his slave tailor's house.
When an extra man followed the Prophet to Abu Shu'aib's meal for five, the Prophet left it to the host to admit or refuse him, and he admitted him.
The Prophet picked gourd from a tailor's soup; Aisha said sacrifice meat was kept fifteen days; the family never ate wheat bread with meat their fill three days running.
The Prophet ate fresh dates with cucumber; Abu Huraira's share of dates from him included a hard, unripe one; and when he died, dates and water had sufficed them.
When a Jew refused Jabir more time on a date debt, the Prophet walked the garden and ate there, and the dates plucked repaid the debt with some left over.
The date palm is like a Muslim; seven morning Ajwa dates guard against poison and magic; never two dates at once without leave; the Prophet ate them with cucumber.
Umm Sulaim's porridge from one mudd of barley fed forty men whom the Prophet called in by tens, and Anas looked to see if it had lessened.
